content: I'm running on an old laptop, using Mint Xfce, so performance is a bit of an issue. I'm working thru 'Mathematics in Lean', but every time VSCode restarts, it takes forever. Are there any settings that could improve this? I appreciate there maybe trade offs.
How many gigs of ram do you have? If 8 or less then you are doomed to slowness I'm afraid. And is mathlib fully compiled, i.e. did you install Mathematics In Lean correctly?

Thanks. 8 unfortunately. I presume it's installed correctly as it works ok, if with a bit of a lag sometimes, and I never shut the machine down, just sleep. But sometimes it doesn't wakeup properly, or VSCode can occasionally just hang, and then its a restart.

How can I tell if it is fully compiled?

One of the ways is to check in vscode itself.
When you open a Lean file that starts with import Mathlib, look at the left margin (gutter) next to the line numbers. If it processes quickly, and no yellow/orange strip, you should be fine, check for errors.
You may also check with lake build as a command on the root directory of your project, if it spins up your CPU, and takes sometime, -> it starts compiling Mathlib now. Or you can check with lake exe cache get .

You can run lake build in a terminal and look at the output. But the answer to your question is that 8 gigs is not enough in 2026 to have a comfortable Lean experience, unfortunately. If you have 16 and you're dealing with mathlib or something downstream like Mathematics In Lean then it's best to close all other memory hogs like web browers before starting. I've been using 32 for years and then the experience is pleasant even with other things open. This is apparently what progress looks like.

There is one more trick that Mathematics in Lean could use, namely moving to the module system. In my experience, that makes a substantial difference w.r.t. memory usage. @Patrick Massot @Jeremy Avigad Would a PR migrating MIL be welcome?
Yes, unless this really makes things confusing for beginners (but I don't see how this could be). Don't hesitate to dm me after opening such a pr.
Kevin, I've been using only 16 gigs of memory forever up until literally a week ago (with a browser and a bunch of tabs). It's totally doable if your OS isn't a memory hog.
OK, thanks for the data point! But what do you think about 8?

Jireh Loreaux said:

Kevin, I've been using only 16 gigs of memory forever up until literally a week ago (with a browser and a bunch of tabs). It's totally doable if your OS isn't a memory hog.

16 is a lot. For some reason we are still in an era where base model laptops come with 8GB of memory and recent memory price rises haven't helped.

Kevin Buzzard said:

OK, thanks for the data point! But what do you think about 8?

we know based on this data that mathlib should be buildable under 8
keep in mind that the module system basically halfed mathlib maxrss
Aha, my prejudices might be pre-module-system.
@Michael Rothgang Mathematics in Lean has no internal imports: the files only depend on Mathlib, not on each other. How can the module system help?

My understanding is that the memory usage require to process (e.g.) import Mathlib in a downstream project is much lower when that project uses the module system. We are now at the point (for six or nine months already) where a bare import Mathlib would make a machine with 8GB of RAM run out of memory. Halving that footprint (as alluded to above) would certainly allow this to continue.
I know MIL doesn't do import Mathlib, but allowing users with only 8GB of RAM to run the files locally seems beneficial to me.

My understanding is that the memory usage require to process (e.g.) import Mathlib in a downstream project is much lower when that project uses the module system

that is correct

Since you already use Linux, my experience don't count here: I have an old laptop from 2017 which has 8G RAM, recently I switched from Windows to WSL and I feel a huge speedup even if there is an overhead when VSCode starts up WSL (about 10 seconds).

Kevin Buzzard said:

OK, thanks for the data point! But what do you think about 8?

as Michael mentions above, 8 without the module system is pretty much untenable these days. I scraped by with 8 on my laptop until 2024, and then realized I could upgrade to 16 even though the official spec for that machine says in no uncertain terms that it cannot support 16 (lies).

(Specifically, import Mathlib when not in the module system imports/loads all of the private data from each module as well. You use less memory with module + import Mathlib because you just ask for the public data, and so are literally loading less into memory :) By now, the public interface of all of Mathlib’s modules should be sufficient for it to behave normally.)

Monitoring the memory usage it became apparent that the default Mint swapfile was way too small, 2GB. Up'ed it to 16GB, maybe overkill, but general performance is way better and has cured the sleep problems. MIL still takes over an hour to load, but because sleep works ok, I don't have to do it anywhere near as often.
Is your disk HDD or SSD?
HDD
That's unfortunate, but HDD will be much slower than SSD...
It certainly is. Moved project folders onto external SSD and it opens in under 5 mins. Thanks
